title: Supersymmetric Moduli, Seiberg–Witten Data and Duality Questions

items.title: Classical and quantum supersymmetric vacuum-moduli data
items.design_state: Step 1 carrier, proof/source contract, and scoped checks complete; item readiness is ready.
items.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ in four-dimensional rigid, global
$\mathcal N=1$ gauge-model data. Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex
Hermitian vector space of scalar field values, let a compact Lie group $G$ act
unitarily on $V$, and fix an orthonormal complex basis
$(\phi^1,\ldots,\phi^n)$ of $V$. Choose Hermitian matrices
$T_a$ for the infinitesimal action of a basis of the Lie algebra of $G$, a
gauge coupling $g>0$, and a gauge-invariant holomorphic polynomial
$W:V\to\mathbb C$. Assume canonical scalar kinetic energy and no
Fayet--Iliopoulos term. Define the auxiliary-field maps

$$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{kin}}=-\sum_i\partial_\mu\overline{\phi^i}\,\partial^\mu\phi^i,\qquad [\phi^i]=\mathrm{mass},\quad [W]=\mathrm{mass}^3,\quad [g]=1.$$

$$F_i(\phi)=\frac{\partial W}{\partial\phi^i}(\phi),\qquad D_a(\phi)=-g\,\phi^\dagger T_a\phi.$$

The tree-level scalar potential is

$$V_{\mathrm{tree}}(\phi)=\sum_{i=1}^n|F_i(\phi)|^2+\frac12\sum_a D_a(\phi)^2.$$

Thus $F_i$ and $D_a$ have mass dimension two and $V_{\mathrm{tree}}$ has
mass dimension four.

A **classical supersymmetric vacuum configuration** is a constant scalar
configuration $\phi\in V$ for which every $F_i(\phi)$ and every
$D_a(\phi)$ is zero. Its **classical vacuum-moduli set** is the topological
orbit space

$$\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cl}}=\{\phi\in V:F_i(\phi)=0\text{ for all }i,\ D_a(\phi)=0\text{ for all }a\}/G.$$

where two configurations are identified exactly when they lie in the same
compact-$G$ orbit, and the set has the quotient topology. The stability
convention here retains every such compact-group orbit, including singular
orbits. No quotient by the complexified group, geometric-invariant-theory
stability criterion, or smooth-manifold structure is included in this
definition.

For a **specified, already constructed quantum theory** $\mathcal T$, suppose
there is a Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, a unitary translation representation
$U(a)$, and densely defined supercharges $Q^I$ and their Hilbert adjoints on a
common domain $\mathcal D$. A **quantum supersymmetric vacuum ray** is the
phase-equivalence class $[\Omega]$ of a normalized vector $\Omega\in\mathcal D$
satisfying
$U(a)\Omega=\Omega$ for every spacetime translation $a$ and
$Q^I\Omega=(Q^I)^*\Omega=0$ for every supercharge $I$. The **quantum
vacuum-moduli set** $\mathcal M_{\mathrm q}(\mathcal T)$ is the set of these
rays, with the topology, if any, supplied by the constructed theory. This
definition is conditional on normalizable invariant vacuum vectors and a
specified quantum Hilbert-space model. It asserts no path-integral measure,
continuum limit, nonperturbative existence, or equality between
$\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cl}}$ and $\mathcal M_{\mathrm q}(\mathcal T)$.

items.title: Pure N=2 SU(2) Coulomb-branch and period data
items.design_state: Step 1 carrier, proof/source contract, and scoped checks complete; item readiness is escalated on the exact prerequisite in its current record.
items.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$, spacetime $\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with metric
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and a selected pure four-dimensional
rigid $\mathcal N=2$ Yang--Mills model whose global gauge group is $SU(2)$.
The matter-hypermultiplet representation set is empty. In $\mathcal N=1$
language the gauge sector is one vector multiplet and one adjoint chiral
multiplet with scalar $\phi\in\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)$; the selected
action convention uses the $\sqrt2 g$ vector--chiral coupling, a positive
dimensionless gauge coupling $g$, and no mass parameter. The earlier model
postulate fixes the $SU(2)$ gauge group, superspace/action conventions, and
coupling normalizations, but its current statement also includes one
hypermultiplet in an arbitrary finite-dimensional unitary representation.
It does not supply the empty-matter condition used here. The pure-model
selection and its full action are therefore an additional conditional input;
this Definition does not derive them from the current one-hypermultiplet
postulate.

A **classical Coulomb-branch configuration** is a constant adjoint scalar
configuration satisfying the model's zero auxiliary-field conditions, taken
modulo the compact $SU(2)$ gauge action. This uses the compact-group orbit
quotient in the preceding vacuum-moduli definition; it does not replace that
quotient by a complexified-group stability construction. In the
weak-coupling semiclassical frame, let $a$ be the eigenvalue coordinate fixed
by $\phi=\operatorname{diag}(a,-a)$, of mass dimension one. When a quantum
theory with a vacuum-moduli set has actually been constructed, the **quantum
Coulomb-branch coordinate** $u$ denotes the chosen gauge-invariant chiral
quadratic-operator expectation value in the source trace normalization for
which the weak-coupling relation is $u=a^2/2$. Its mass dimension is two.
This definition does not assert that $u$ globally parameterizes the quantum
vacua.

On an open patch $U$ of the $u$-plane where the period functions are
holomorphic and the local gauge-coupling matrix has positive imaginary part,
an **electric/magnetic frame** means a chosen ordered basis of the formal
charge lattice that fixes local cycle representatives. Their period
functions are the complex electric coordinate $a:U\to\mathbb C$ and complex
dual coordinate $a_D:U\to\mathbb C$, both of mass dimension one. The local
two-derivative abelian gauge action is encoded by a holomorphic
**prepotential** $\mathcal F_U(a)$ of mass dimension two, defined on that
patch by

$$a_D=\frac{\partial\mathcal F_U}{\partial a},\qquad \tau=\frac{\partial a_D}{\partial a}=\frac{\partial^2\mathcal F_U}{\partial a^2},\qquad \operatorname{Im}\tau>0.$$

The dimensionless $\tau$ is the local complexified gauge coupling; changing
the electric/magnetic frame changes the pair $(a_D,a)$ by the corresponding
integral linear transformation and may require a different local
prepotential. Thus neither period is asserted to be a single-valued global
function on a punctured branch.

For this source-normalized data, define the **formal electric/magnetic charge
label lattice** to be $\Gamma_{\mathrm{SW}}=\mathbb Z^2$, with a label
$(n_e,n_m)$ and period pairing
$\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{SW}}(u;n_e,n_m)=n_ea(u)+n_ma_D(u)$. The pair labels
the central-charge formula; the lattice definition does not assert that every
label is an allowed line operator, a dynamical particle, a stable state, or a
state in any constructed Hilbert space. Those are separate model data.

The word **exact** in this page refers only to the adopted source-proposed
Wilsonian two-derivative low-energy data on a regular patch of the selected
pure SU(2) model. It does not mean a proof of a nonperturbative continuum
path integral, a global single-valued prepotential, or an exact statement
about arbitrary $\mathcal N=2$ theories.

items.title: Local dual U(1) monopole-Higgs effective data
items.design_state: Step 1 carrier, proof/source contract, and scoped checks complete; item readiness is escalated on the exact prerequisite in its current record.
items.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$, metric
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and the local duality frame near one
monopole singularity of the selected pure $SU(2)$, four-dimensional rigid
$\mathcal N=2$ model. Let $A_D$ be the complex scalar coordinate in the
local dual $U(1)_D$ vector multiplet, and let $M,\widetilde M$ be complex
scalar fields of dual electric charges $+1$ and $-1$ in two $\mathcal N=1$
chiral multiplets. The current batch 31 N=2 model postulate instead specifies
one hypermultiplet in an arbitrary finite-dimensional unitary representation;
it does not supply the pure, empty-matter ultraviolet model assumed by this
local patch. This local effective data is conditional on a separately
specified matching pure-model input and is not derived from that current
postulate. The dual gauge group acts by

$$A_D\mapsto A_D,\qquad M\mapsto e^{i\alpha}M,\qquad \widetilde M\mapsto e^{-i\alpha}\widetilde M,\qquad \alpha\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z).$$

Let $u(A_D)$ be the supplied holomorphic coordinate function on an open
patch $|A_D|<r$ about $A_D=0$, with $u(0)=u_m$ and
$c:=u'(0)\ne0$. Let $\mu\ne0$ be the coefficient of the small adjoint
mass perturbation, let $g_D>0$ be the dimensionless dual gauge coupling,
and use canonical scalar kinetic terms and zero Fayet--Iliopoulos parameter.
Define

$$W_\mu(A_D,M,\widetilde M)=\sqrt2 A_D M\widetilde M+\mu u(A_D),\qquad D=g_D\bigl(|M|^2-|\widetilde M|^2\bigr).$$

$$V_\mu=|\partial_{A_D}W_\mu|^2+|\partial_M W_\mu|^2+|\partial_{\widetilde M}W_\mu|^2+\frac12D^2.$$

Let $\widetilde F_{\mu\nu}=\partial_\mu\widetilde A_\nu-
\partial_\nu\widetilde A_\mu$ and
$\widetilde D_\mu A_D=\partial_\mu A_D$,
$\widetilde D_\mu M=(\partial_\mu-i\widetilde A_\mu)M$, and
$\widetilde D_\mu\widetilde M=(\partial_\mu+i\widetilde A_\mu)
\widetilde M$. In metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, the
canonical bosonic kinetic Lagrangian is

$$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{kin}}=-\eta^{\mu\nu}\left(\partial_\mu\overline{A_D}\,\partial_\nu A_D+\overline{\widetilde D_\mu M}\,\widetilde D_\nu M+\overline{\widetilde D_\mu\widetilde M}\,\widetilde D_\nu\widetilde M\right)-\frac{1}{4g_D^2}\widetilde F_{\mu\nu}\widetilde F^{\mu\nu}.$$

The mass dimensions are
$[A_D]=[M]=[\widetilde M]=[\mu]=\mathrm{mass}$,
$[u]=\mathrm{mass}^2$, $[W_\mu]=\mathrm{mass}^3$,
$[F_{A_D}]=[F_M]=[F_{\widetilde M}]=[D]=[\widetilde F_{\mu\nu}]=\mathrm{mass}^2$,
$[\widetilde A_\mu]=\mathrm{mass}$,
$[c]=\mathrm{mass}$, and $[g_D]=1$. The allowed regime is restricted to
field values within this patch and energies below its stated effective
cutoff; “small $\mu$” means that the induced scale
$(|\mu c|/\sqrt2)^{1/2}$ lies well below that cutoff.

This is a one-singularity effective data package. It includes neither a
simultaneously local electric description of mutually nonlocal dyons nor a
claim that the local action extends over the full moduli space. A finite-energy
vortex is not part of this Definition; its existence, when needed, is a
separate hypothesis.

items.title: Finite-energy dual-Higgs flux-tube sector
items.design_state: Step 1 carrier, proof/source contract, and scoped checks complete; item readiness is escalated on the exact prerequisite in its current record.
items.statement:
Use the dual $U(1)_D$ fields and potential of the preceding local
monopole-Higgs model. Let $x^1,x^2$ be coordinates on the transverse plane
$\mathbb R^2$ and let $x^3$ be the coordinate along a straight static tube.
Write $\widetilde A_i$ for the spatial dual gauge potential,
$\widetilde F_{12}=\partial_1\widetilde A_2-\partial_2\widetilde A_1$,
$D_iM=(\partial_i-i\widetilde A_i)M$, and
$D_i\widetilde M=(\partial_i+i\widetilde A_i)\widetilde M$.

A **finite-energy dual vortex profile of winding $n$** is a smooth static
configuration $(A_D,M,\widetilde M,\widetilde A_1,\widetilde A_2)$ on
$\mathbb R^2$ for which the transverse energy

$$\sigma=\int_{\mathbb R^2}\left(\frac{\widetilde F_{12}^2}{2g_D^2}+|D_iM|^2+|D_i\widetilde M|^2+V_\mu-V_{\mathrm{vac}}\right)\,d^2x$$

is finite. The fields approach a supersymmetric vacuum at infinity satisfying
$A_D=0$, $|M|=|\widetilde M|=v>0$,
$\sqrt2 M\widetilde M+\mu u'(0)=0$, and
$V_{\mathrm{vac}}=0$. The phase map $M/|M|$ restricted to a sufficiently
large circle has degree $n\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$ as a map to the unit
circle; the phase map $\widetilde M/|\widetilde M|$ has degree $-n$.
Require also that $D_iM$ and $D_i\widetilde M$ tend to zero on that circle,
that the tangential component of $\widetilde A-d\arg M$ tends uniformly in
$\theta$ to zero as the circle radius tends to infinity, and that the
limiting flux exists. The profile is a translation-invariant
tube along $x^3$; its tension is the transverse integral $\sigma$. This
Definition includes no assertion that such a configuration exists or is a
stationary solution of the field equations.

In the adopted electric/magnetic frame, the **original electric flux** of
this sector means the dual magnetic flux
$\Phi_D=\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_{|x|\le R}\widetilde F_{12}\,d^2x$.
The flux dictionary is part of the selected duality model; this Definition
does not state that every electric line charge is represented by a vortex.
In natural units, $[\widetilde A_i]=\mathrm{mass}$,
$[\widetilde F_{12}]=\mathrm{mass}^2$, and
$[\sigma]=\mathrm{mass}^2$.

items.title: Source-proposed pure SU(2) N=2 Seiberg–Witten low-energy data
items.design_state: Step 1 carrier, proof/source contract, and scoped checks complete; item readiness is escalated on the exact prerequisite in its current record.
items.statement:
Adopt the source-proposed low-energy solution data for pure four-dimensional
rigid $\mathcal N=2$ Yang--Mills with global gauge group $SU(2)$, one
adjoint vector multiplet, rank one, no matter hypermultiplets, and the coupling,
$\sqrt2$ vector--chiral interaction, units, and prepotential convention of
the selected N=2 vector-multiplet model. Use natural units
$c=\hbar=1$, metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and a positive
dynamical scale $\Lambda$ of mass dimension one. The gauge-invariant
coordinate $u$ has mass dimension two; set $w=u/\Lambda^2$.

The current batch 31 N=2 model postulate specifies one hypermultiplet in an
arbitrary finite-dimensional unitary representation and does not supply the
no-matter condition adopted here. The pure-model field content remains a
separate conditional input; this postulate does not infer it from the current
one-hypermultiplet carrier.

On the regular $w$-plane with singular values $w=1,-1,\infty$ removed,
adopt the family of genus-one curves, where $x,y,w$ are dimensionless:

$$\Sigma_w:\quad y^2=(x-1)(x+1)(x-w).$$

and the meromorphic period differential

$$\lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}=\frac{\sqrt2\Lambda}{2\pi}\frac{y\,dx}{x^2-1}.$$

Within this proposed solution, take the quantum vacuum-moduli data to be the
entire $u$-plane, with a $\mathbb Z_2$ symmetry $u\mapsto-u$ and singular
values $u=\Lambda^2,-\Lambda^2,\infty$. This is part of the adopted
solution ansatz, not a consequence of a constructed continuum theory.

For a chosen local cycle basis $\gamma_m,\gamma_e$ on $\Sigma_w$ with
intersection number $\gamma_m\cdot\gamma_e=1$, define
$a_D=\oint_{\gamma_m}\lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}$ and
$a=\oint_{\gamma_e}\lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}$. These periods have mass
dimension one, are multivalued under continuation around the punctures, and
are used in the local prepotential convention
$a_D=\partial\mathcal F/\partial a$ and
$\tau=\partial^2\mathcal F/\partial a^2$ with
$\operatorname{Im}\tau>0$. In the source's counterclockwise-loop
convention, the period column $(a_D,a)^T$ has monodromy matrices

$$M_\infty=\begin{pmatrix}-1&2\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad M_+=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\-2&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad M_-=\begin{pmatrix}-1&2\\-2&3\end{pmatrix}.$$

Adopt the source's formal charge-label lattice $\mathbb Z^2$ and central-charge pairing
$\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{SW}}=n_ea+n_ma_D$ for labels
$(n_e,n_m)\in\mathbb Z^2$. In the supersymmetry convention of this page,
the scalar central charge is normalized as
$z=\sqrt2\,\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{SW}}$. The mass inequality and its
saturation statement are separate theorem deductions. No claim is made that
every lattice label is an allowed line operator or is represented by a stable
particle.

Adopt the singularity interpretation that the $w=1$ point has a light
monopole with $a_D=0$, while the $w=-1$ point has a light dyon with
$a-a_D=0$ in the chosen frame. These are source-proposed physical inputs
tested by their monodromies; they are not deduced here from a constructed
continuum theory.
In the local monopole patch, use the dual $U(1)_D$ data from the preceding
effective-model definition. A small N=1-breaking mass parameter $\mu$ of
mass dimension one adds the local superpotential term $\mu u(A_D)$ to
$\sqrt2 A_D M\widetilde M$. The local description applies only near this
singularity, below its effective cutoff, and does not simultaneously describe
the mutually nonlocal dyon at the other singularity.

Here **exact low-energy solution** means the adopted two-derivative
Wilsonian data of this source-defined model on its regular patches. It does
not mean a proof of a nonperturbative UV path integral, a global
single-valued prepotential, or an identity for arbitrary gauge groups,
matter contents, or N=2 theories.

items.title: N=2 SU(2) central-charge mass bound from Seiberg–Witten periods
items.design_state: Step 1 carrier, proof/source contract, and scoped checks complete; item readiness is escalated on the exact prerequisite in its current record.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Use the four-dimensional rigid
$\mathcal N=2$ super-Poincare convention
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, $\epsilon_{12}=1$, and
$c=\hbar=1$. Let $U$ be a regular patch of the selected pure-SU(2)
Seiberg--Witten period data. Fix $u\in U$ and a formal charge label
$(n_e,n_m)\in\mathbb Z^2$. Suppose the selected physical model has a
nonzero massive unitary rest-fiber representation $\mathcal K$ with mass
$M>0$, scalar central-charge matrix $Z^{12}=zI$, $Z^{21}=-zI$, a common
dense invariant product domain $\mathcal D$, and actual Hilbert adjoints for
all supercharges. Require its charge normalization to be

$$z=\sqrt2\,\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{SW}}(u;n_e,n_m)=\sqrt2\bigl(n_ea(u)+n_ma_D(u)\bigr).$$

Then

$$M\ge\sqrt2\,|n_ea(u)+n_ma_D(u)|.$$

If equality holds, choose $\varphi\in\mathbb R$ with
$e^{-i\varphi}z=|z|$ and define
$A=Q^1_1-e^{i\varphi}(Q^2_2)^*$ and
$A^\sharp=(Q^1_1)^*-e^{-i\varphi}Q^2_2$ on $\mathcal D$. Both
$A\psi$ and $A^\sharp\psi$ vanish for every $\psi\in\mathcal D$.
Equality defines algebraic BPS saturation only; the statement asserts no
state exists for any chosen charge label and no BPS state is stable.

items.title: Flux quantization and positive tension for an admitted dual vortex
items.design_state: Step 1 carrier, proof/source contract, and scoped checks complete; item readiness is escalated on the exact prerequisite in its current record.
items.statement:
Use the local dual $U(1)_D$ model with natural units, positive coupling
$g_D>0$, smooth gauge potential on $\mathbb R^2$, and the vortex boundary
conditions of the preceding definition. If a finite-energy dual vortex
profile of winding $n\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$ exists, then its dual
magnetic flux, which is the original electric flux in the adopted duality
frame, is

$$\Phi_D=2\pi n,$$

and its transverse tension satisfies $0<\sigma<\infty$. This is a
conditional statement about an admitted profile; it asserts neither
existence nor stability of any vortex or a linearly confining minimum-energy
potential between external charges.

items.title: Conditional monopole Higgs vacuum after a small N=1 perturbation
items.design_state: Step 1 carrier, proof/source contract, and scoped checks complete; item readiness is escalated on the exact prerequisite in its current record.
items.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$, metric
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and the local monopole patch of the
selected pure-SU(2) N=2 source-proposed low-energy model. Let $u(A_D)$,
$c=u'(0)\ne0$, $M$, $\widetilde M$, $g_D$, and $\mu$ be the data in the
local dual-Higgs definition, with $\mu\ne0$ and
$(|\mu c|/\sqrt2)^{1/2}$ well below the effective cutoff. Restrict to a
neighborhood of $A_D=0$ on which $u'(A_D)\ne0$. The supersymmetric vacuum
equations in this patch have exactly one $U(1)_D$ gauge orbit, represented
by

$$A_D=0,\qquad M\widetilde M=-\frac{\mu c}{\sqrt2},\qquad |M|=|\widetilde M|=v:=\left(\frac{|\mu c|}{\sqrt2}\right)^{1/2}>0.$$

Thus the local monopole fields have nonzero gauge-fixed amplitudes and
$U(1)_D$ is fully Higgsed. With the canonical kinetic normalization of the
local model, the dual vector mass is

$$m_D^2=2g_D^2\bigl(|M|^2+|\widetilde M|^2\bigr)=4g_D^2v^2>0.$$

For the confinement conclusion, make the following additional explicit
effective-model assumption: for a fixed nonzero original electric test-charge
sector and every sufficiently large separation $L$, the minimum-energy
configuration in that sector is a straight, translation-invariant dual
vortex of nonzero winding as defined here, and its endcap energy is bounded
uniformly in $L$. If that flux-tube sector exists, its original electric
flux is quantized and its tension is positive; the corresponding potential
has $V(L)=\sigma L+O(1)$, where $O(1)$ denotes a term bounded uniformly as
$L\to\infty$. This is linear confinement only in the stated local effective
model and under the stated vortex/minimization assumption. The theorem does
not prove that a vortex exists or minimizes the energy.

items.physical_scope: Conditional local effective-model deduction near one pure-SU(2) N=2 monopole singularity after a small N=1 perturbation; the F/D vacuum and dual U(1) Higgs mass are proved, while linear electric confinement additionally assumes a minimizing finite-energy vortex sector and bounded endcaps. No UV continuum or framework-wide confinement claim is made.

title: Supersymmetric Moduli, Seiberg–Witten Data and Duality Questions — Examples

items.title: One-flavor U(1) classical F/D-flat vacuum quotient
items.design_state: Step 1 carrier, proof/source contract, and scoped checks complete; item readiness is ready.
items.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Take the finite-dimensional scalar field
space $V=\mathbb C^2$ with coordinates $(q,\widetilde q)$, standard
Hermitian norm, compact gauge group $U(1)$ acting by
$(q,\widetilde q)\mapsto(e^{i\alpha}q,e^{-i\alpha}\widetilde q)$, gauge
coupling $g>0$, zero superpotential $W=0$, canonical scalar kinetic terms,
and zero Fayet--Iliopoulos parameter. In the tree-level model the auxiliary
maps are $F_q=F_{\widetilde q}=0$ and
$D=-g(|q|^2-|\widetilde q|^2)$. The classical supersymmetric vacuum set is
therefore
$\{(q,\widetilde q):|q|=|\widetilde q|\}/U(1)$. The gauge-invariant
coordinate $m=q\widetilde q$ gives a bijection of this orbit set with
$\mathbb C$. This is a classical tree-level result and is not a claim about
the quantum vacuum space.

references.title: David Tong, Supersymmetric Field Theory
references.locator: §4.3.1, printed pp. 112–116: zero-FI one-flavor U(1) SQED D-term condition, gauge quotient, and gauge-invariant meson coordinate.

items.physical_scope: Exact classical tree-level calculation for a canonical rigid four-dimensional N=1 U(1) gauge-model example with one oppositely charged chiral pair, zero superpotential, and zero Fayet–Iliopoulos parameter; it says nothing about quantum corrections.

items.title: SU(Nf) cubic-anomaly check for proposed SQCD dual data
items.design_state: Step 1 carrier, proof/source contract, and scoped checks complete; item readiness is ready.
items.statement:
Let integers $N_c\ge2$ and $N_f$ satisfy
$\frac32N_c<N_f<3N_c$, and put $\widetilde N_c=N_f-N_c$. Consider the
following proposed four-dimensional $\mathcal N=1$ SQCD field data, in
natural units. In the electric $SU(N_c)$ theory, there are $N_f$ quark
chiral multiplets $Q$ in the fundamental of the flavor group
$SU(N_f)_L$, with $N_c$ color copies; the antiquark multiplets are singlets
under $SU(N_f)_L$. In the proposed magnetic $SU(\widetilde N_c)$ theory,
the quark multiplets $q$ are in the antifundamental of $SU(N_f)_L$, with
$\widetilde N_c$ color copies, and the meson multiplet $M$ transforms in
$(\mathbf N_f,\overline{\mathbf N_f})$ under
$SU(N_f)_L\times SU(N_f)_R$, giving $N_f$ copies of the fundamental of
$SU(N_f)_L$. The magnetic antiquarks and both gauginos are
$SU(N_f)_L$ singlets. Normalize the cubic-anomaly coefficient of a
left-handed Weyl fermion to $+1$ in $\mathbf N_f$ and $-1$ in
$\overline{\mathbf N_f}$, and add coefficients over independent copies.
Then the electric and proposed magnetic $SU(N_f)_L^3$ coefficients are

$$\mathcal A_{\mathrm{electric}}=N_c,\qquad \mathcal A_{\mathrm{magnetic}}=-(N_f-N_c)+N_f=N_c.$$

This equality is one anomaly-matching consistency check of the proposed
field data; it is not a proof of Seiberg duality or of equality of the
infrared continuum theories.

references.title: N. Seiberg, Electric-Magnetic Duality in Supersymmetric Non-Abelian Gauge Theories
references.locator: §3, printed pp. 6–8, especially equations (3.1)–(3.4): proposed magnetic field representations and the SU(Nf) cubic-anomaly matching table.

references.title: David Tong, Supersymmetric Field Theory
references.locator: §6.5.1, printed pp. 198–200: electric/magnetic field representations and the SU(Nf)L^3 anomaly calculation; the discussion calls the checks evidence, not a proof of duality.

items.physical_scope: Algebraic anomaly-coefficient check for the proposed four-dimensional N=1 electric/magnetic SQCD field data in the conformal window; it is not evidence that the two continuum theories are equivalent.

items.title: Symbolic monopole vacuum in the local dual U(1) model
items.design_state: Step 1 carrier, proof/source contract, and scoped checks complete; item readiness is escalated on the exact prerequisite in its current record.
items.statement:
In the local dual $U(1)_D$ model, let $u(A_D)$ be holomorphic near
$A_D=0$, let $c=u'(0)\ne0$, and choose a neighborhood small enough that
$u'(A_D)\ne0$ throughout. Choose a nonzero small perturbation
$\mu$ for which $(|\mu c|/\sqrt2)^{1/2}$ is below the effective cutoff.
The supersymmetric vacuum equations have the gauge orbit represented by

$$A_D=0,\qquad M=v>0,\qquad \widetilde M=-\frac{\mu c}{\sqrt2v},\qquad v=\left(\frac{|\mu c|}{\sqrt2}\right)^{1/2}.$$

At this representative $|M|=|\widetilde M|=v$, so the D equation vanishes.
The dual $U(1)_D$ is fully Higgsed and the canonical dual vector mass is
$m_D^2=4g_D^2v^2>0$. This is a symbolic local effective-model calculation.
The example does not assert existence of a finite-energy vortex or linear
confinement; the zero-perturbation case $\mu=0$ is outside its scope.
